episodes.about: Kevin Roose's new book, The AGI Chronicles, tells the story of the AI revolution. He joins the show to explain its earliest beginnings: the researchers who discovered what language models could do, the people who debated whether humans or computers are more special, and the executives who started the companies that currently rule our economy. What do they want, and what are they building?
episodes.title: Inside the early days of the AI revolution
episodes.why: Kevin Roose tells the early history behind his new book The AGI Chronicles: the researchers who found what language models could do and the executives who built the companies now ruling the economy.

episodes.about: Reid Hoffman and Aria Finger weigh in on AI policy heading into the midterms, from Bernie Sanders and Greg Casar's proposal to ban superintelligence to Anthropic's own frontier AI safety bill. They map the political coalitions forming around AI regulation, including a bipartisan push from Chris Murphy and Josh Hawley to hold developers liable when AI agents hack. Reid explains why pausing AI for a congressional process would be a mistake. They also examine Satya Nadella's call to treat AI models as potential insider risks, the public feud between Factory and Cognition, and whether VCs can still back competing AI startups.
episodes.title: AI’s midterm coalitions, Anthropic’s safety bill, and VC conflicts
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Possible is Reid Hoffman's weekly show on what AI makes newly possible, new here: Hoffman and Aria Finger map the midterm coalitions forming around AI, from a proposed superintelligence ban to Anthropic's own safety bill.

episodes.about: Mark Cuban thinks AI could transform healthcare, but it won't fix opaque prices and broken incentives on its own. His starting point for employers: run every benefits contract through AI and ask where you're getting ripped off. Mark joins a16z General Partner Julie Yoo and Erik Torenberg to discuss what he's learned building Cost Plus Drugs, why trust is its core product, and how greater transparency could put pressure on healthcare costs. They also explore where AI can help, what personalized medicine could look like, how the role of doctors may change, and why Mark believes founders should use AI to learn, not as an excuse to stop thinking.
episodes.title: Mark Cuban’s Plan to Make Healthcare Affordable
episodes.why: Out today: Mark Cuban says AI won't fix healthcare prices on its own, but employers should run every benefits contract through AI to find where they are getting ripped off.

episodes.about: Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang join Latent Space to explain the engineering behind the Claude Platform: launching Opus 5.5, separating the model's “brain” from the agent's “hands,” scaling APIs, and building reliable managed agents.
episodes.title: How Anthropic ships the #1 LLM in the World safely: Separating the Brain from the Hands
episodes.why: Anthropic's Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang explain how the Claude Platform ships Opus 5.5 safely: separating the model's brain from the agent's hands, scaling the API, and making managed agents reliable.

episodes.about: Meta's new AI agent Muse is one of the fastest-growing apps ever. It's a big bet from a company spending billions to win the AI race. But what is the real cost of using this powerful, free AI product?
episodes.title: Why Meta is giving you Muse for free
episodes.why: Meta's AI agent Muse is one of the fastest-growing apps ever and it is free; The Indicator asks what the real cost of using it is.
